# Draft:WIN WIN Gothenburg Sustainability Award

WIN WIN Gothenburg Sustainability Award
Introduction
The WIN WIN Gothenburg Sustainability Award is an international sustainability prize based in Gothenburg, Sweden. Established in 2000, the award recognizes individuals, organizations, and movements that develop innovative solutions to global sustainability challenges. Each year the prize highlights a new theme connected to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. The main award includes a monetary prize of 1 million SEK, and in 2018 the organization introduced the WIN WIN Youth Award, aimed at encouraging young changemakers worldwide.
History
The award was founded in 2000 by a coalition of public institutions, regional actors, and civil society organizations in Gothenburg, with the aim of promoting long-term sustainability solutions. Over the years, the themes have reflected a broad spectrum of global challenges, including climate change, poverty reduction, biodiversity, human rights, and circular economy.
In 2018, the Youth Award was launched to recognize people aged 13–29 who contribute to sustainable development in their communities or globally. Both awards are accompanied by seminars, public events, and educational activities held throughout the year.
Laureates
Since its inception, the WIN WIN Award has honored a wide range of global leaders, innovators, and activists. Past laureates include Al Gore, Kofi Annan, Gro Harlem Brundtland and Bellingcat among others.
Each year’s laureate is selected based on relevance to the annual theme, proven impact, and alignment with the UN Sustainable Development Goals. The Youth Award similarly highlights young individuals or groups who have demonstrated significant positive influence within the theme area.
Organisation
WIN WIN is operated as a non-profit association funded by the City of Gothenburg, the Västra Götaland Region, and a network of member organizations. The association is governed by an annual general assembly, which appoints a board responsible for strategic direction and financial oversight.
Two independent juries—one for the main award and one for the Youth Award—evaluate nominees and select the laureates. The juries are supported by annually appointed expert advisors and a theme organization with specialized knowledge relevant to that year’s focus. Day-to-day operations are managed by a secretariat.
Impact
The award aims to increase awareness of sustainable development challenges and highlight practical solutions that can be scaled globally. Through conferences, seminars, public dialogues, and educational initiatives, WIN WIN functions as a platform for knowledge exchange between academia, policymakers, business leaders, and civil society.
Many laureates have gained increased international visibility, new collaboration opportunities, and expanded outreach as a result of the award. The organization also contributes to public understanding of sustainability through continuous communication efforts, youth engagement programs, and international partnerships.
